newsitem.title: PERU: Small explosion shakes Peru soccer stadium.
newsitem.headline: Small explosion shakes Peru soccer stadium.

text.p: A small explosion caused by dynamite shook a soccer stadium on the outskirts of the southern Peruvian city of Arequipa late on Tuesday, causing some damage but no injuries, police said.
Eight youths were arrested outside the stadium after the explosion at 7.40 p.m. (0040 GMT).

Police said the explosion might have been the work of the Marxist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA). "It could be the action of the MRTA, but it is too early to tell," police official Alberto Gutierrez told Reuters.
The MRTA has threatened reprisal attacks for the government military strike last week against 14 rebels holding 72 hostages for more than four months at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.

Local radion station Cadena Peruana de Noticias reported that there had been people inside the stadium during the day celebrating the end of the hostage crisis in which all the MRTA rebels were slain and all but one of their captives released alive.
But Gutierrez said the stadium was empty when the dynamite exploded.
